subject: Continuity assurance deep-dive: Aurora Health DR/RTO-RPO Q&A

Hi Markus,

Thanks for the quick intro earlier this week. As part of Aurora's procurement packet we need a more detailed write-up on Redwood's disaster recovery and business continuity posture covering: RTO and RPO commitments by deployment mode, multi-region failover sequencing (active/active vs warm-standby), how cache/state is recovered, expected failover window for large model artifacts, testing cadence and evidence, and any constraints around data residency.

I attached our standard questionnaire template (Aurora_DR_QA_Template.xlsx) — can you please populate or provide a narrative response we can include in the RFP?

Appreciate it — Elena

Elena — thanks for sending the template and for the clear list. Below is a concise narrative we can include in your packet; I'm attaching a short overview and a runbook summary for quick reference. If you need tabular answers for the spreadsheet, we can fill that out as well.

High level commitments (per deployment mode):
- Hosted (shared): Target RTO: failover to warm regional pool within 1–3 minutes for stateless API traffic; RPO: near-zero for persisted artifacts (cross-region replicated storage), best-effort for in-flight sequences.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): Target RTO: 30–120 seconds depending on model size and pre-warmed capacity profile; RPO: sub-30s for persisted checkpoints when checkpointing is enabled; replicable to near-zero for model artifacts.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): RTO/RPO depend on customer configuration; Redwood provides runbooks and orchestration tooling for active/active or active/passive patterns — we will document expected windows based on the chosen architecture.

Failover patterns and sequencing:
- Active/Active: Preferred for low-latency requirements. Traffic is routed by our smart routing layer with per-route policies; cross-region load balancing is used with consistent hashing for session affinity. RTO in this setup is effectively immediate for new requests; tail latencies may vary by region.
- Active/Passive (Warm standby): We maintain pre-warmed capacity in secondary regions and a two-phase cutover (health-check based drain + routing switch). Expected cutover window: 60–180s depending on model weights and KV-cache warmup.

State, cache, and model artifact handling:
- Model artifacts are stored in an object store with cross-region replication and versioned snapshots. Artifact promotion to serving nodes is parallelized; large model boot times are reduced via snapshot sharing and pre-fetching.
- KV/prefix caches are warmed using a replay loader and pre-populated prefix sets when a customer opts into warm-standby. For short-lived sessions, we provide best-effort replay from replicated request logs.

Testing and evidence:
- Quarterly automated smoke failovers (synthetic traffic) and annual full DR exercises with customers on Dedicated/Private.
- We can provide redacted postmortem excerpts and a runbook extract showing the test plan and successful cutover timestamps.

Security and controls:
- All artifacts and backups are encrypted in transit and at rest (KMS-managed keys).
- Audit logs for failover actions and routing changes are retained per customer retention policy; we can provide audit slices for procurement review.

Next steps: I'll loop in Karthik (serving runtime lead) and Laura (ops) for the technical appendix and specific numbers for the Dedicated profile. Attached: Redwood_DR_Overview.pdf and Redwood_Runbook_Summary.docx.

Best,
Markus
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

2) Describe how you avoid split-brain or duplicate processing during route switch.
3) For multi-region backups, what are typical replication lag figures and retention windows?
4) Please confirm whether any customer data (logs, prompts) are ever stored outside the configured region without explicit opt-in.

If Karthik or Laura can include short, technical answers for these four points it would help us close the loop.

Elena — jumping in with the technical appendix for your four points. Below are concise, procurement-ready bullets we typically include in RFP responses. Happy to expand any item.

1) Failover times for large models (70B example):
- Cold start (no pre-warmed containers, model pulled from cross-region object store): full readiness 8–18 minutes depending on network and instance startup; we report conservative upper bounds in contracts.
- Warm standby (pre-warmed GPU pool with model already loaded): failover and traffic acceptance typically 30–120 seconds. Time variance driven by model sharding and KV-cache rebuild.

2) Preventing split-brain / duplicate processing:
- Smart routing uses a central control plane for coordinated routing changes combined with per-region health checks. Cutover follows a two-phase protocol: (a) global routing controller marks primary as draining and signals edge proxies to stop new sessions, (b) once active sessions drain or hit a configurable timeout, controller flips traffic to standby and confirms health probes. All routing events are logged and audited.
- For stateful workloads we rely on idempotency tokens and sequence numbers at application layer; we expose guidance for customer integrations to avoid duplicate side effects.

3) Replication lag and retention:
- Artifact replication (object storage): cross-region replication typically completes within seconds to low tens of seconds for small artifacts; full model promotion (hundreds of GB) is parallelized and can complete in minutes. We publish SLA bands for artifact promotion per model size in the Dedicated contract appendix.
- Telemetry/log shipping: near-real-time via replicated streams; expected lag <60s under normal conditions, with retries and backpressure handling.
- Retention: default 90 days for operational logs, configurable up to multi-year per enterprise agreement; snapshot retention for model artifacts configurable (30/90/365 days).

4) Data residency and storage boundaries:
- By default, customer data and logs are stored in the region you configure for the deployment. Cross-region replication of artifacts and telemetry only occurs if enabled in the customer's account or as part of a contractual DR setup. We do not replicate or store prompts/logs outside the configured region without explicit opt-in.

Testing and evidence notes:
- We maintain redacted sample runbooks and time-stamped test evidence for procurement. For Dedicated customers we offer joint DR exercises and can provide post-test artifacts (logs, metrics traces) under NDA.

Ping me if you need precise numbers for the 70B model on a specific instance family — we can run a quick warm-start measurement in our staging fleet.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Principal, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
